segments.speaker: Rob Moore
segments.words: Bert Gamble was raised near Genesee, Idaho. His lifelong fascination with the region and his consuming regard for rendering it inverse have gained him the sobriquet the poet of the Palouse. On this trip, Bert reads many problems from the collection Days of Yesterday and Songs of the Palouse Country. He reads beautifully. He reads with passion. He is carried off by sadness and laughs when the humorous moment takes him. He is a joy to listen to. It is recommended that you read the poems as he speaks them, because he sometimes exchanges or substitutes for words in the text.

And if you, you're ever down around the roundhouse or whether moving locomotive, you will see what I'm talking about, you will see the, the wonderful way they have a moving equipment, you know, on it's great. Well, what is it?

segments.speaker: Rob Moore
segments.words: This is Sharon's Rose.

segments.speaker: Daniel (Bert) Gamble
segments.words: Sharon's Rose Oh, Sharon's Rose, yes, yes. Christ says in the Bible "I am the rose of Sharon." Roses live only a summer, roses live only a day, buds that bloom in happy springtime, blossom only to decay; but within the heavenly portal, where eternal love abides, blows the spiritflower immortal, far beyond the sunset tides. Spiritflower you bloom forever, in that land beyond the skies, snows of time shall kiss you never, in that far-off paradise; gates of heaven lend protection, you grow dearer every hour, symbol of our resurrection, angels bless you, spiritflower. That is really the name of the spiritflower. Well, I'm so happy that you got out and that you brought the book with you. Yes, and...

segments.speaker: Rob Moore
segments.words: Are there a couple letters you particularly like to read?

segments.speaker: Daniel (Bert) Gamble
segments.words: Well, if there's something there that you like, I'd be happy to do.

segments.speaker: Rob Moore
segments.words: Well I like almost all of them.

segments.speaker: Daniel (Bert) Gamble
segments.words: Oh, Glenn, I think you wonderful.

segments.speaker: Rob Moore
segments.words: Why don't you read the last one here in the book?

segments.speaker: Daniel (Bert) Gamble
segments.words: I will. This is a kind of a gruesome thing. Faith that triumphs — I'm dead now, I'm dead, this is after death — Wrapped in my snowy shroud I lie, formaldehyde in my veins — just ask a doctor what he does with formaldehyde; he pumps it into your veins after death and that preserves you. Yes, oh yes, here we are, yes, yes: I hear you not when you come to cry over these cold remains. I do not know that the roses nod, outside the lonely room, of the fresh, dark earth in the churchyard sod, cleft for my silent tomb. But remember if I could speak to you, "Heart of mine" these lips would say, "The power that has blessed me my long life through Will wake me again someday." Faith Triumphant. And here's one called Easter: [aside: The doctor that's doing all this doctoring — his father is a minister and he's a wonderful good, good man. He read for me at Easter and said a prayer for me and wept for me and cried at Easter. He was a good man. Oh yes, thank you, thank you]. This is the victory that overcometh, now has the stone been rolled away, this is the blossom blowtime glorious, Wonderful Resurrection Day. Many or few will be the years remaining, it matters not if his love abides, and the faith of the Christ of God's ordaining,Rrisen anew with Eastertide. That's Easter, an Easter prayer. Well if you ever met this doctor, this man died two days after Easter, and he was a good, good man. He cried with me, held my hand, prayed for me and recited a prayer, and he was a grand and good man. Do you ever get up to the university?

segments.speaker: Rob Moore
segments.words: Occasionally, yes

segments.speaker: Daniel (Bert) Gamble
segments.words: There's a university library is available there and anytime that you happen to be up there, you want to feel welcome to go into that library there and The Days of Yesterday is there And that's what it's for, it's for you to read and your loved ones to read and enjoy.

segments.speaker: Rob Moore
segments.words: Would you like to read the poem, Days of Yesterday, since the book's named for it?

segments.speaker: Daniel (Bert) Gamble
segments.words: That's an idea. Days of Yesterday. Out of the gateway of yesterday, the covered wagons wend, out of the golden long ago, silently end to end. Down the sunflower slopes and bunch grass trails, they passed me in bold array Then my soul leaped up and I'm young again, In my days of yesterday. I love to recall the pioneers that in tender memories sleep, theirs was the struggle that we might live, the sowing that we might reap; So in sweet daydreams Let me ride once more up those bunch grass trails away, in my chaps and spurs with the pioneers in those days of yesterday; And in after years, when I hit the road that their kindly feet have trod, it will lead my steps aright, I know, up that bunch grass trail to God

segments.speaker: Rob Moore
segments.words: Okay, are there any more you would particularly like to read?

segments.speaker: Daniel (Bert) Gamble
segments.words: No, I think we've picked them all up

segments.speaker: Rob Moore
segments.words: Okay, well let's call it quits for now. We can both take a break and think about it

segments.speaker: Daniel (Bert) Gamble
segments.words: Please do, and let me find a way to thank you for your

segments.speaker: Rob Moore
segments.words: Let me write the title down here

segments.speaker: Daniel (Bert) Gamble
segments.words: Your lovely visit, it's been an inspiration. It's just been an inspiration to hear your voice. And I am deeply grateful for all you've said to me and done to make it pleasant

segments.speaker: Rob Moore
segments.words: I'm really glad you enjoyed the visit so much.

segments.speaker: Daniel (Bert) Gamble
segments.words: Oh, bless you, bless you Then you will come again.

segments.speaker: Rob Moore
segments.words: Yes, I will, I will

segments.speaker: Daniel (Bert) Gamble
segments.words: God bless you and do come again real soon.
